claims.text: An elemental Cr coating provides baseline corrosion protection to zirconium-alloy cladding.
The proposed intervention is Al-ion implantation at approximately 1×10^16 ions/cm² and 200 keV followed by controlled annealing.
Post-implantation annealing can promote Al segregation without degrading the Cr-coating microstructure.
Al implantation and annealing will form a nanometric Al-enriched barrier at the Cr/Zr interface.
During annealing, implanted Al atoms will migrate to the Cr/Zr interface.
Interfacial Al will form a thermodynamically stable Al-rich phase or mixed Cr–Al oxide.
The Al-rich interfacial phase will block fast diffusion paths and lower the effective Cr–Zr interdiffusion coefficient.
The barrier will significantly slow Zr diffusion into Cr at elevated temperature.
The modified coating will retain the corrosion protection associated with Cr under normal reactor-water conditions.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the treated coating will have a significantly lower Cr–Zr interdiffusion rate during high-temperature steam exposure.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will delay coating failure during approximately 1200 °C steam transients.
The treated coating will have corrosion resistance comparable to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline during approximately 320 °C subcritical-water exposure for up to 60 days.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during short accident-relevant steam exposures at approximately 1200 °C.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during subcritical PWR-water exposure at approximately 320 °C for up to 60 days.
